steps.announcement: Begin basic bubble sort on six elements.
steps.explanation: No comparisons have been made. All six elements [4, 1, 3, 1, 5, 2] at indices 0 through 5 are in the first pass's unsorted range [0, 5].
steps.key_state: Initially, the array is [4, 1, 3, 1, 5, 2], the range to process is [0, 5], and no suffix is fixed.
steps.title: Before the first pass

steps.announcement: Pass 1 is complete. The 5 is fixed at index 5, leaving [0, 4].
steps.explanation: Pass 1 compares neighbors and swaps as needed from left to right in [0, 5], moving the maximum, 5, into place at index 5. The next pass covers only the remaining range [0, 4].
steps.key_state: After pass 1, the array is [1, 3, 1, 4, 2, 5]. Index 5 is fixed, leaving [0, 4].

steps.explanation: Pass 2 compares and swaps within [0, 4], moving the maximum of this range, 4, to index 4. The fixed suffix on the right grows to [4, 5]. The remaining range is [0, 3].
steps.key_state: After pass 2, the array is [1, 1, 3, 2, 4, 5]. Indices 4 through 5 are fixed, leaving [0, 3].

steps.announcement: Pass 3 is complete. The 3 is fixed at index 3. The array is sorted, but processing continues on [0, 2].
steps.explanation: Pass 3 moves 3 into place at index 3 within [0, 3]. The entire array [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] is now in ascending order. Without an early-exit flag, the basic version continues checking [0, 2].
steps.key_state: After pass 3, the array is [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. Indices 3 through 5 are fixed, leaving [0, 2]. The array is sorted, but the basic version continues looping.

steps.announcement: Pass 4 makes no swaps. The 2 is in place at index 2, leaving [0, 1].
steps.explanation: Pass 4 scans [0, 2]. All neighbors are already in order, so no swaps occur. The 2 at index 2 is confirmed in place, leaving [0, 1].
steps.key_state: After pass 4, the array is [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. Indices 2 through 5 are fixed, leaving [0, 1].

steps.announcement: Pass 5 makes no swaps. Only one element remains in [0, 0], and sorting is complete.
steps.explanation: Pass 5 compares the two 1s in [0, 1]. No swap is needed, confirming that the 1 at index 1 is in place. Only a single minimum, 1, remains in [0, 0]. No further comparison is needed, and all five passes are complete.
steps.key_state: After pass 5, the array is [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. Indices 1 through 5 are fixed. The remaining range [0, 0] contains just one element, so sorting is complete.

prose.summary: The six animation steps show the initial state and the states after passes 1 through 5. The step number differs from the pass number.
prose.title: Bubble sort pass by pass

context: Initially nums = [4, 1, 3, 1, 5, 2], with indices 0 through 5. Each pass compares neighbors from left to right in the unsorted range (the “remaining range” in the table). Swapping when the left value is larger moves the maximum to the right end of the range. Later passes skip the fixed suffix.
description: The array is in ascending order after pass 3. This basic version has no early-exit flag, so passes 4 and 5 still run without making any swaps. The table shows the entire array initially and at the end of each pass.

frames.explanation: After five passes, only the minimum, 1 at index 0, remains. It needs no further comparison.
frames.title: Bubble sort pass by pass

summary: Each pass fixes the largest remaining value in place, growing the sorted suffix on the right.
